title: Reduce console backend tail latency with grouped-request middleware, resolver fast-path, and adaptive cache-hints
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: High-level: The Console backend is exhibiting elevated tail latency (p95/p99) during bursts of traffic from dashboards and the rollouts page. This ticket implements a three-pronged cleanup: 1) add a grouped-request middleware to coalesce simultaneous identical REST/GraphQL requests at the proxy layer; 2) split GraphQL resolvers into fast-path (simple, cached reads) and slow-path (heavy joins/transformations) to reduce blocking on the event loop; 3) introduce adaptive cache-hints and short-lived in-memory prefix cache for hot keys. This is primarily a tech-debt/perf cleanup to lower variance and cost without changing public APIs.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for dashboard list endpoints reduced by >=25% and p99 reduced by >=20% under synthetic burst tests (see perf-dashboard link)
Group-middleware reduces duplicate backend calls for identical live queries by >=50% on average in production traces
GraphQL fast-path implemented behind a feature flag with no functional regressions and unit/contract tests in CI
Adaptive cache-hints added to top 10 hot resolvers; cache hit rate improvement visible in Console observability dashboards
Change gated by feature flag and rollout to 10% of traffic before full rollout; rollback path documented
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha: Triage: confirmed tail latency spikes during 12:00–13:00 PST in staging and prod. Linked perf dashboard and flamegraphs. Decided to attack request duplication and resolver hot paths first.

2026-02-22 - Marcus: Spike complete — implemented prototype grouped-request middleware in the API-proxy (Node). Locally reduces duplicate downstream requests by ~65% for identical simultaneous queries. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4281

2026-02-25 - QA: Ran synthetic burst test with 200 concurrent dashboard viewers — p99 improved from 980ms -> 680ms when grouped-request enabled but observed an outlier when slow-path resolver hit external indexer. Need resolver split.

2026-03-02 - Design decision: split resolvers into 'fast' and 'composed' categories. Fast resolvers must be pure reads with <2 SQL joins and no heavy JSON transforms. Composed resolvers scheduled on worker pool with increased timeout. Document: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Console+Resolver+Fast+Path

2026-03-05 - Security review: no new surface; caching is short-lived and respects auth tokens. Security note: ensure cache keys include token scoping where necessary. @security-team approved (see thread).

2026-03-08 - Marcus: Upgraded redis client from ioredis 5.2 -> 6.0 to enable v4 cluster pipelining. Minor API changes addressed in PR 4302. Impact: lower tail during heavy cache miss storms. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4302

2026-03-09 - Observability: Added histogram buckets at 10ms, 50ms, 200ms, 500ms, 1s for proxy grouped-request latency. Early data shows grouped-request adds median 2ms overhead but reduces downstream duplicate load significantly.

2026-03-10 - Marcus: In-progress: feature-flag rollout scheduled. Smoke tests green in staging. Planning 10% canary on 2026-03-12. Follow-up items: refine prefix cache TTLs and add metric for 'requests_coalesced' per route.
